refnamediv.refpurpose: plot multiple timeseries on time axis

refsynopsisdiv.title: Syntax
refsynopsisdiv.synopsis: stackedplot // demo stackedplot(ts) stackedplot(ts1, ..., tsN) stackedplot(..., vars) stackedplot(..., LineSpec) stackedplot(..., LineSpec, GlobalProperty) stackedplot(..., "CombineMatchingNames", %f) stackedplot(..., Name, Value) stackedplot(axes_handle, ...) ax = stackedplot(..)

listitem.para: strings vector containing to variables names of timeseries
column index vector corresponding to position in variables names timeseries
cell of strings: each element can contain one or multiple variables names.

This optional argument must be a string that will be used as a shortcut to specify a way of drawing a line. We can have one LineSpec per y or {x,y} previously entered. LineSpec options deals with LineStyle, Marker and Color specifiers (see LineSpec). Those specifiers determine the line style, mark style and color of the plotted lines.

This optional argument represents a sequence of couple statements {PropertyName,PropertyValue} that defines global objects properties applied to all the curves created by this plot. For a complete view of the available properties (see GlobalProperty).
'Title': string that contains the title of plot.
'DisplayLabels': matrix of strings that contains the names of Y-label for each axe. Default value: variables names of timeseries
'LegendLabels': matrix of strings that contains the names of timeseries.

This optional argument forces the stackedplot to replace the axes given by axes_handle rather than the current axes (see gca). If axes_handle belongs to a stackedplot, all the axes of this stackedplot are replaced.
A vector of handle(s) to the axes created.

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: The stackedplot function plots selected variables of one or more timeseries objects in a set of vertically stacked axes sharing the same time basis. All timeseries objects passed to a single call must have the same time basis.

When two or more input timeseries have common variable names, their curves are combined in the same graph by default. With "CombineMatchingNames", %f, a separate graph is created for each variable of each timeseries.

Several independent stackedplot objects can be created in the same figure. The stacked axes replace the current axes, so stackedplot can be used after subplot to build stacked plots in different sub-regions of the same figure. Each axes created by stackedplot is tagged "stackedplot:group:rank": when the current axes belongs to a stacked plot, the whole stacked plot is replaced. Axes belonging to another subplot are preserved.

stackedplot(..., vars) plots only variables of timeseries specified by vars. vars can be
a vector of strings containing variables names to plot.
a vector of indexes corresponding to position of variables names in timeseries.
a cell containing variable names in matrices to plot them in same graphs. ie: {"var1", ["var2", "var3"]} will display var1 in a graph and var2 and var3 in another one.
stackedplot(..., LineSpec, GlobalProperty) customizes the line style, marker or color of polylines. This arguments are the same as the plot function.
stackedplot(..., "Title", str) adds a plot title.
stackedplot(..., "DisplayLabels", str) specifies the labels for the y-axis.
stackedplot(..., "LegendLabels", str) adds a legend for each plot. str is a vector of size N timeseries input. The legend can be used to specify the name of timeseries.
stackedplot(..., "CombineMatchingNames", %f) disables the default grouping of variables having the same name across input timeseries.
Enter the command stackedplot to see a demo.
